message.text: I'm checking usage of the two Runner declarers: memopayload's RunOnce and NewRunner appear unused anywhere, including tests, while s3presign's RunOnce is actually invoked from server.go and internally within its own Run method. I'm now searching for any test references to RunOnce to confirm this pattern.

h08.

**Two types declare `RunOnce`, and only one of them is ever invoked.**

- `*s3presign.Runner` — `server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:43` — **yes, invoked** — `server/server.go:163` (inside `startBackgroundRunners`, for the immediate pass at startup), and internally by its own ticker loop at `server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:36`.
- `*memopayload.Runner` — `server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:27` — **no, never invoked** — no caller in production or test code.

On the dead one: a repo-wide search for `memopayload` returns only three hits outside its own file, all in `server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go` — the import at line 18 and two calls to the package-level function `memopayload.RebuildMemoPayload` at lines 108 and 447 (used when creating and updating a memo). The `Runner` type's constructor `memopayload.NewRunner` (line 19) has no callers either, so nothing ever builds an instance on which `RunOnce` could be called. The method is a bulk backfill that would walk every memo in batches of 100 and rewrite its payload; it appears to be leftover migration machinery, since the per-memo work it does is now performed inline by the two `RebuildMemoPayload` calls in the API handlers.

I also checked `internal/scheduler`, which is the other place a `RunOnce`-style hook might be declared or required by an interface; it has no such method, so the two above are the complete set.
